title: RSI-Forge: From Research Papers to Environments for Recursive Self-Improvement
abstract: Environments are the foundation of recursive self-improvement: they provide the problems agents work on and the feedback used to evaluate progress. Yet constructing challenging research environments with reliable evaluation still depends on domain experts, limiting their scale and disciplinary coverage. We introduce RSI-Forge, a multi-agent pipeline that turns published papers into executable environments for self-improvement. Three agents coordinate construction, reproduction, and review to produce tasks with automated evaluators; each paper's method is independently reimplemented to establish a baseline score. We present 210 environments across 18 fields, including 90 reviewed by independent human domain experts. Both experts and agent judges give high ratings to the potential for improving the provided starting solutions and the evaluators' ability to distinguish solution quality, whereas experts are more critical of shortcut resistance, faithfulness to the source paper, and whether a single idea can exhaust a task. To validate their use for repeated improvement, we evaluate four models over 3 successive attempts on 120 environments, with each attempt inheriting prior code and notes while model weights remain fixed. At least one model improves after the first attempt in 84% of environments. Models also outperform the reproduced paper methods in 68 of the 120 environments, demonstrating room for gains beyond these baselines. Transcript analysis identifies work beyond parameter tuning in 95% of these successful attempts. Analysis of the resulting trajectories shows that models scoring lower on these tasks explore less, more often accept gains smaller than the reported standard error, and rely more heavily on tuning to the development set. RSI-Forge provides a scalable approach to constructing research environments for training and evaluating self-improving agents.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Today's lecture is on R-S-I-Forge. In our graduate seminar on research agents, we keep returning to a practical question: how can we tell whether an agent has improved a research solution? Recent work such as Agent-as-a-Judge and Training A-I Scientists to Replicate Research reflects growing interest in evaluating agent work and reproducing science. R-S-I-Forge takes a related but distinct direction: it uses published papers to build runnable tasks and independent reference solutions. I see a hand—yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 今天的讲座是关于R-S-I-Forge的。在我们研究智能体的研究生研讨课上，我们一直在反复讨论一个实际问题：我们怎么判断一个智能体是否改进了某个研究方案？最近的一些工作，比如Agent-as-a-Judge和Training A-I Scientists to Replicate Research，反映出人们对评估智能体工作和复现科学的兴趣日益增长。R-S-I-Forge走的是一个相关但不同的方向：它利用已发表的论文来构建可运行的任务和独立的参考解决方案。我看到有人举手——是的，Noah？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi, Professor. Is the central idea mainly to give agents more time to solve research problems?
segments.zh: 教授您好，它的核心思路主要是给智能体更多时间来解决研究问题吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Not quite. The paper starts from a bottleneck: evaluating research improvement requires both a challenging task and a trustworthy way to score solutions, and building those usually takes scarce expert and engineering effort. R-S-I-Forge divides that work among agents with separate responsibilities. Its collection contains 210 environments across 18 fields. The goal is to make repeated changes to solutions measurable, not to claim that the agents have advanced the original scientific research.
segments.zh: 不完全是。这篇论文的出发点是这样一个瓶颈：要评估研究上的改进，既需要一个有挑战性的任务，也需要一种可信赖的方式来给解决方案打分，而构建这些通常要耗费稀缺的专家和工程精力。R-S-I-Forge 把这项工作拆分给各司其职的多个智能体。它的数据集包含 18 个领域的 210 个环境。目标是让对解决方案的反复修改变得可衡量，而不是声称这些智能体推进了原本的科学研究。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The pipeline begins with an author agent, which adapts a paper’s method and research question into a bounded task. It prepares a starting solution, data-generation code, an evaluator, and separate development and held-out test sets. A reviewer checks whether the instructions are usable and whether the evaluator measures the stated objective. When checks fail, the task can go back for repair; accepted tasks are not simply one-shot generations.
segments.zh: 这条流水线从作者智能体开始，它把论文的方法和研究问题改造成一个有边界的任务，准备好初始解法、数据生成代码、评估器，以及彼此分开的开发集和留出测试集。审核智能体会检查指令是否可用、评估器是否真的在衡量既定目标。检查不通过时，任务可以退回修复；被接受的任务并不是一次性生成就完事的。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Quick question: what makes the reproduced method an independent baseline rather than just another starting solution?
segments.zh: 快速问一下：是什么让复现出来的方法成为一个独立的基线，而不只是另一个起始方案？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: A reproducer implements the paper’s method independently using solver-facing materials, without access to the author agent’s implementation or construction history. It also does not receive the test data or target score. Its implementation is evaluated on held-out data as a separate reference point. The starting solution scores 0, and a task-specific target defines 1; that target helps normalize scores but is not necessarily attainable. Of the accepted main-run environments, 79% needed at least one revision.
segments.zh: 复现者只依据面向求解器的材料独立实现论文方法，接触不到作者智能体的实现或构建过程，也拿不到测试数据和目标分数。其实现会在留出数据上评估，作为一个独立的参照点。起始方案得分为0，任务特定的目标定义为1；这个目标用于归一化分数，但不一定可达。在通过筛选的主实验环境中，79%至少需要一次修订。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That distinction matters when interpreting the solver study. Four models each made 3 successive attempts on 120 environments from the main run. A new session inherited earlier code and notes, but began with a fresh context; the model weights stayed fixed. At least one model improved by 0.01 or more in normalized score after the first session in 84% of environments. At least one surpassed the reproduced baseline in 68 of 120.
segments.zh: 这一区分在解读求解器研究时很重要。四个模型各自对主实验中的120个环境连续做了3次尝试。新会话会继承之前的代码和笔记，但会以全新的上下文开始；模型权重保持不变。在84%的环境中，至少有一个模型在第一次会话后归一化分数提升了0.01或更多。在120个环境中有68个，至少有一个模型超过了复现的基线。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So does beating that baseline mean the agent discovered a better scientific result?
segments.zh: 那这是否意味着，超过该基线就代表智能体发现了更好的科学成果？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: No. These are gains on bounded tasks adapted from papers, not evidence of progress on the original research problems. The study measures changes to task solutions, not learning in model weights or general research ability. Also, 95% of sessions that beat the reproduced baseline were coded as involving work beyond parameter tuning. But that category includes repairs and evaluating alternatives, and the transcript labels were generated by a model without human validation; it cannot establish scientific novelty.
segments.zh: 不能。这些只是在改编自论文的有限任务上取得的提升，并不能证明在原始研究问题上取得了进展。这项研究衡量的是任务解法的变化，而不是模型权重中的学习或通用研究能力。此外，在击败复现基线的会话中，有95%被编码为涉及参数调优之外的工作。但这一类别包括修复和评估替代方案，而且转录标签是由模型生成的，未经人工验证，因此无法确立科学新颖性。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Human review adds another view of what these environments can and cannot measure. Experts rated room for improvement above a starting solution at 4.81 out of 5 and score discrimination at 4.74. The three-judge panel’s corresponding means were 4.89 and 4.65. But experts rated resistance to saturation lower, at 3.09, compared with the panel’s 3.98. Saturation asks whether one idea might exhaust a task; it is a distinct concern from whether scores separate stronger solutions.
segments.zh: 人工评审提供了另一个视角，来看这些环境能测什么、不能测什么。专家对“相比初始方案还有多大改进空间”的评分是4.81分（满分5分），对“分数区分度”的评分是4.74分。三位评审对应的均值分别是4.89和4.65。但专家对“抗饱和性”的评分更低，只有3.09，而评审小组给了3.98。饱和性问的是，一个想法是否可能把某个任务做到头；这和分数能否区分更强方案是两回事。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Can we treat those rating gaps as evidence that the judges were too generous?
segments.zh: 我们能把这些评分差距当作评委过于宽松的证据吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Not on their own. Experts reviewed 90 of the 180 main-run environments, one expert per environment, and did not receive exactly the same evidence as the agent judges. Experts also rated shortcut resistance and fidelity to the source paper more critically. These are judgments about rubric dimensions, not direct proof that every evaluator is valid. The comparison is useful as a diagnostic, while its differences in evidence and limited expert coverage need to stay visible.
segments.zh: 光凭这些还不够。专家审查了180个主实验环境中的90个，每个环境由一位专家负责，而且他们拿到的证据和智能体评审并不完全相同。专家对捷径抵抗性和对源论文忠实度的评分也更严格。这些判断针对的是评分标准中的各个维度，并不能直接证明每个评估者都有效。这种比较作为诊断工具是有用的，但它在证据上的差异以及专家覆盖范围有限的问题，仍需被清楚地看到。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The paper also compares ratings with R-S-I-Exam, which evaluates repeated improvement on executable research tasks. On different, unpaired task sets, the same three agent judges rated R-S-I-Forge higher for score discrimination and shortcut resistance, but lower for resistance to saturation. That contrast does not isolate the effect of automated construction. More broadly, the paper contributes a process for building and inspecting tasks; the result does not show that automation itself makes an environment better.
segments.zh: 论文还把评分和R-S-I-Exam做了对比，后者评估的是在可执行研究任务上的反复改进。在不同的、非配对的任务集上，同样的三个智能体评审给R-S-I-Forge在分数区分度和抗捷径性上打了更高的分，但在抗饱和性上打了更低的分。这一对比并没有分离出自动化构建本身的效果。更广泛地说，论文贡献的是一套构建和检查任务的流程；结果并不表明自动化本身就能让环境变得更好。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: How should we read the example trajectory without overgeneralizing from it?
segments.zh: 我们该如何解读这条示例轨迹，又不至于以偏概全呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: One example follows a Claude Opus 5 agent on a humanoid foothold-selection task. Its three final submissions rise from 0.15 to 0.33 to 0.58 in normalized held-out score. Across sessions, the agent changes how it searches candidate footholds and checks ground support. That illustrates what an inherited solution path can look like, but one trajectory cannot explain the aggregate gains or show which particular change caused them. Some held-out grading material was also accessible during solver runs.
segments.zh: 其中一个例子是Claude Opus 5智能体执行人形机器人落脚点选择任务。它最终提交的三次结果在归一化留出评分上从0.15升到0.33再到0.58。在不同会话中，智能体改变了搜索候选落脚点和检查地面支撑的方式。这说明继承下来的解题路径可能是什么样子，但单条轨迹无法解释整体收益，也无法说明究竟是哪个具体改动带来了这些收益。此外，求解器运行期间还能访问到部分留出评分材料。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The larger implication is a more concrete way to study agent work: construct bounded tasks from published methods, attach an independently reproduced reference, and observe how solutions change across attempts. This complements work focused on judging projects or reproducing papers, while asking a different evaluation question. Future studies can test how robust these environments are, whether their results transfer, and what causes improvement. This study does not establish that inherited records, rather than extra solving time, produced the gains.
segments.zh: 更大的意义在于，它提供了一种更具体的研究智能体工作的方法：从已发表的方法中构建有边界的任务，附上一个独立复现的参考实现，然后观察解决方案在多次尝试中如何变化。这补充了那些专注于评审项目或复现论文的工作，同时提出了一个不同的评估问题。未来的研究可以检验这些环境有多稳健、它们的结果能否迁移，以及改进究竟由什么导致。本研究并不能证明是继承下来的记录、而非额外的求解时间带来了这些提升。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The key takeaway is to separate a measurable improvement on an adapted task from progress in science or self-improvement in a model. R-S-I-Forge offers a multi-agent approach to constructing executable research tasks and comparing solutions against reproduced methods. Its results support using such environments to examine agent behavior, while also exposing questions about fidelity, shortcuts, and saturation. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our A-I assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 关键结论是，要把在适配任务上可测量的改进，与科学进步或模型自我提升区分开来。R-S-I-Forge 提供了一种多智能体方法，用来构建可执行的研究任务，并把解决方案与复现的方法进行比较。它的结果支持用这类环境来考察智能体行为，同时也暴露出关于保真度、捷径和饱和的问题。感谢收听。如果你还有任何问题，可以询问我们的人工智能助手，或者留言评论。
